Implement export function parseCsv(text, options = {}) in src/csv.js (replace the naive stub). options.delimiter is a single character, default ','. Records are separated by LF or CRLF; a lone CR not followed by LF is ordinary data. Empty input returns []. A single line break at the very end of the input does not start another record, but any other empty line is a record with one empty field (so 'a

b' gives [['a'],[''],['b']] and 'a

' gives [['a'],['']]). Fields are never trimmed. A field is quoted only if its FIRST character is a double quote: inside a quoted field, two double quotes produce one double quote, and delimiters, LF and CRLF are kept verbatim as data. After the closing quote the next character must be the delimiter, a line break, or end of input; anything else (including a space) throws a SyntaxError. An unterminated quoted field throws a SyntaxError. A double quote that is not the first character of a field is literal data. Without options.header, return an array of records, each an array of field strings. With options.header === true, the first record is the header row and the result is an array of objects, one per remaining record (header-only or empty input gives []). Each object is a plain object (prototype Object.prototype) whose own enumerable properties are the header names in header order, including names such as '__proto__' which must become ordinary own properties. Duplicate header names throw an Error. A data record whose field count differs from the header throws a RangeError whose message contains 'record N', where N is the 1-based data record number (the header is not counted). Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

Implement src/topo.js: export class CycleError extends Error, and export function topoSort(graph). graph is a plain object mapping a node name to an array of the names it depends on. Every key and every name appearing in a dependency list is a node. Duplicate dependencies are ignored. The input must not be mutated. All string comparisons below use plain JavaScript string ordering (a < b), not numeric order and not object key order. Step 1, cycle check: run a depth-first search starting from each not-yet-visited node in ascending order; from a node, follow its dependencies in ascending order (edge: node -> dependency). The first time the search reaches a dependency that is currently on the DFS stack, throw a CycleError whose cycle property is the stack slice from that dependency to the current node, followed by that dependency again (e.g. {a:['b'], b:['a']} gives ['a','b','a']; a self-dependency x gives ['x','x']), and whose message is 'Cycle detected: ' + cycle.join(' -> '). Reaching an already fully finished node is not a cycle. Any cycle causes the throw, even if other parts of the graph could be ordered. Step 2, ordering (only if there is no cycle): return an array of all nodes in which every node comes after all of its dependencies, built with Kahn's algorithm where, at each step, the next node emitted is the smallest node among all nodes whose dependencies have all been emitted. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

Implement export class WeightedLRU in src/lru.js (replace the stub). Constructor: new WeightedLRU({ maxWeight, ttlMs, now = Date.now, onEvict }). maxWeight and ttlMs must be finite numbers > 0, otherwise throw RangeError. now() returns the current time in ms; onEvict(key, value, reason) is optional. An entry expires when now() >= its insertion time + ttlMs. Expired entries are removed lazily whenever they are encountered, and every such removal calls onEvict(key, value, 'expired'). Methods: set(key, value, weight = 1): weight must be a finite number > 0 of type number, otherwise throw TypeError. If the key already exists, remove it silently first (no onEvict). If weight > maxWeight, return false (the old entry stays removed). Otherwise: first remove ALL expired entries (reported in least- to most-recently-used order), then insert the entry as most recently used with a fresh TTL, then while the total weight exceeds maxWeight evict the least recently used other entry with onEvict(key, value, 'capacity'); return true. get(key): returns the value and marks the entry most recently used; does NOT extend its TTL; returns undefined if missing or expired. peek(key): like get but does not change recency. has(key): boolean, does not change recency. delete(key): removes a live entry silently and returns true; returns false if missing; if the entry is expired it is removed as expired (reported) and false is returned. Getters size and totalWeight, and method keys() (returns keys ordered from most to least recently used), first remove all expired entries. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

Implement src/patch.js: export class PatchError extends Error (with an index property), and export function applyPatch(doc, patch) that applies an array of JSON Patch operations (RFC 6902 semantics) to a JSON document and returns the result. The input doc must never be mutated, and the result must not share any object or array references with doc or with values inside the patch. Operations are applied in order; if any fails, throw a PatchError whose index is the 0-based index of the failing operation (the input stays untouched). JSON Pointer: '' is the whole document; otherwise the pointer must start with '/', is split on '/', and each token is decoded by replacing '~1' with '/' and then '~0' with '~'. Object tokens refer to OWN properties only. Array tokens must be '0' or a decimal integer without leading zeros or sign; '-' (meaning the end of the array) is allowed only as the last token of an add path. Every token except the last must resolve to an existing value. Operations: add (path, value): on an array insert at the index (index may equal the length), '-' appends; on an object set the key; path '' replaces the whole document. remove (path): target must exist; arrays remove the element; removing '' is an error. replace (path, value): target must exist; '' replaces the whole document. move (from, path): from must exist; if path equals from it is a no-op; if path is inside from (path starts with from + '/') it is an error; otherwise it is remove(from) followed by add(path). copy (from, path): from must exist; adds a deep copy at path. test (path, value): fails unless the target is deeply equal to value: arrays element-wise in order, objects with the same set of own keys and deeply equal values regardless of key order, primitives with ===. Any other op name is an error. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

test.mjs is failing. src/pool.js, src/memo.js and src/index.js implement a small async toolkit; read the code, run the test, and fix every defect in src/ so the following contract holds. mapLimit(items, limit, fn): limit must be an integer >= 1, otherwise the returned promise rejects with a RangeError. fn(item, index) may return a promise or a plain value, or throw. The first min(limit, items.length) calls start synchronously, in index order, before mapLimit returns. Whenever a call fulfills, the next unstarted item starts (in index order); never more than limit calls are in flight. The promise resolves to the results in INPUT order (not completion order). Empty input resolves to [] without calling fn. If any call rejects or throws, the returned promise rejects with that same reason and no further items are started (calls already in flight are not cancelled). memoizeAsync(fn, { key }) returns memoized(...args); the cache key is key(...args), default String(args[0]); keys are arbitrary strings, including names like 'constructor', 'toString' and '__proto__'. On a cache miss fn is invoked synchronously, during the memoized call. memoized always returns a promise; concurrent calls with the same key return the very same promise; fulfilled results are cached; a rejection (including a synchronous throw from fn) is NOT cached, so the next call retries. When a promise rejects, its cache entry is removed only if it is still the entry stored for that key (a stale rejection must not evict a newer entry created after clear). memoized.clear(key) removes one key; memoized.clear() removes all. createFetcher in src/index.js composes the two and must keep working. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

src/chars.js and src/text.js are buggy with non-ASCII text. Fix them so that, everywhere, a 'character' means one Unicode code point (a surrogate pair is one character; a lone surrogate is also one character). chars.js: charLength(s) returns the number of characters; chars(s) returns the array of characters; isAttachedMark(ch) is true exactly when the first code point of ch is in U+0300..U+036F inclusive, is U+FE0E or U+FE0F, or is in U+1F3FB..U+1F3FF inclusive. text.js: truncate(s, max, ellipsis = '…'): if s has at most max characters return s unchanged; otherwise, if max is smaller than the character length of ellipsis throw a RangeError, else return the first (max - charLength(ellipsis)) characters of s followed by ellipsis. reverse(s): split s into clusters, where a cluster is one character followed by all attached marks immediately after it (a mark at the very start of the string starts a cluster like any other character); return the clusters in reverse order, each cluster kept intact. wrap(text, width): width must be an integer >= 1, otherwise throw RangeError. Words are the maximal runs of non-whitespace (whitespace as matched by the JavaScript regex \s). Lines are built greedily: a word is appended to the current line, separated by one space, if the resulting line has at most width characters; otherwise the current line is finished and the word starts a new line. A word longer than width first finishes the current line (if non-empty), then is emitted as consecutive lines of exactly width characters; its remaining shorter tail (if any) becomes the current line, to which later words may be appended. Return the array of lines; empty or whitespace-only text returns []. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

Refactor the configuration API in src/. Add export function createConfig({ env = {}, defaults, prefix = 'APP_' }) to src/config.js and export it from src/index.js. It returns { values, get }. values has exactly the content loadConfig(env, defaults, prefix) produces today (same override, coercion, ignore and error rules, including thrown TypeErrors), and is deeply frozen (every nested object and array). The caller's defaults object and anything inside it must not be frozen, modified, or shared with values. get(path, fallback) takes a dot-separated path such as 'db.pool.max' and walks own properties only; it returns fallback (default undefined) when a segment is missing or when a non-object is reached before the path ends; an existing value is always returned, even if it is null. Keep loadConfig(env, defaults, prefix = 'APP_') exported with identical behavior: it must return a fresh, fully mutable object every call, and it must reuse the same implementation as createConfig rather than a second copy (the error text 'expected a boolean' must appear exactly once in src/config.js). Migrate src/server.js and src/worker.js to createConfig, reading values through get('...'); they must no longer reference loadConfig. serverSettings(env) and workerSettings(env) must return exactly what they return today, as plain mutable data (callers may push to the returned cors array). Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.

weeklyReport in src/report.js produces wrong reports; test.mjs fails. Read src/dates.js, src/money.js, src/sort.js and src/report.js, run the test, and fix the defects so this contract holds. isoWeek('YYYY-MM-DD') returns { year, week } per ISO-8601: weeks start on Monday, week 1 is the week containing the year's first Thursday, and year is the ISO week-numbering year (so dates near New Year can belong to the previous or next year); the result must not depend on the host time zone. weekKey(date) returns 'YYYY-Www' with the week zero-padded to two digits (e.g. '2026-W05'). parseCents(amount) converts an exact decimal string to integer cents with no floating-point error; valid input is an optional '-', one or more digits, and optionally '.' followed by one or two digits ('3' -> 300, '1.5' -> 150, '0.57' -> 57, '-0.57' -> -57); anything else (including '', '1.', '.5', '1.234', '1e2', surrounding spaces) throws a TypeError. formatCents(cents) returns a string with exactly two fraction digits. sortBy(items, keyFn, { descending }) returns a NEW array sorted by the numeric key, does not modify items, and is stable (equal keys keep their input order, in both directions). weeklyReport(entries), with entries [{ date, amount }], returns one row { week, total, count } per ISO week, total formatted with formatCents, sorted by total descending, rows with equal totals in the order their week first appears in entries; entries must not be mutated. Do not modify test.mjs or package.json.
